1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.

2. None appears on behalf of the respondent no.2.
3.
In terms of the F.I.R., it was stated that the daughter of the informant was enticed away by the applicant.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant argued that even at the time of lodging the F.I.R., the victim was pregnant carrying a fetus of 19 weeks.
As regards the age, it is argued that as per the educational record, the tentative age of the victim is around 16 years.
He further argued that no process for final adjudication of the age of the victim has been adopted so far.

1 ready to undertake to solemnise the marriage with the victim.
The statement to that effect has been made in the present bail application.
Hence, the applicant who is languishing in jail since 6.3.2023 having no criminal history, may be enlarged on bail.
5. Learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail.

6. Considering the fact the applicant is undertaking to solemnise the marriage with the victim coupled with the fact that the applicant who is languishing in jail since 6.3.2023 having no criminal history, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
7. Accordingly, the application for grant of bail is allowed.

8. Let the applicant Babu @ Subhash be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No.80 of 2023, under Sections 363, 366, 352, 504, 376, 506 I.P.C. and Section 5j(2)/6 of the POCSO Act, Police Station Sandila, District Hardoi on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.20,000/-
each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions :-
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
9.
